title: Adjectives
description: Learn adjectives for Grade 6: kinds of adjectives, position, and the three degrees of comparison — with bilingual notes, examples, practice exercises and online tests.

topics.title: Kinds of Adjectives & Position
topics.concept:
Adjectives do different jobs:

KindTells usExample
Descriptive (Quality)what kinda brave soldier
Quantitativehow muchsome water
Numeralhow many / orderthree boys, the first day
Demonstrativewhich onethis book, those cars
Possessivewhosemy pen
Interrogativeasks about a nounwhich road?

Position: an adjective is attributive before the noun (a beautiful garden) or predicative after a linking verb (the garden is beautiful).

examples.problem: Is the adjective attributive or predicative? The soup smells delicious.

recap: Adjectives tell what kind, how many, which one, or whose
Attributive = before the noun; predicative = after a linking verb
Demonstratives (this/that/these/those) also act as adjectives before a noun

topics.title: Degrees of Comparison
topics.concept:
Adjectives change form to compare. There are three degrees: positive (one), comparative (two), superlative (three or more).

  • Short adjectives (1 syllable): add -er / -est — tall, taller, tallest.
  • Spelling: big→bigger; happy→happier (y→i); late→latest (drop e).
  • Long adjectives (2+ syllables): use more / most — beautiful, more beautiful, most beautiful.
  • Irregular: good→better→best; bad→worse→worst; many/much→more→most.

Use than with comparatives and the with superlatives: She is wiser than her brother; she is the wisest in class.

examples.solution: easier, easiest — consonant + y changes to i before -er/-est.

recap: Short adjectives add -er/-est; long ones use more/most

intro.en: An adjective describes or adds information to a noun or pronoun. It tells us what kind, how many, which one, or whose. In "a tall boy with two bags," both tall and two are adjectives.
intro.hi: विशेषण (Adjective) किसी संज्ञा या सर्वनाम की विशेषता बताता है। यह बताता है कि वस्तु कैसी है, कितनी है, कौन-सी है या किसकी है। "a tall boy with two bags" में tall और two दोनों विशेषण हैं।

real_life.situation:
At the market your friend asks:

Friend: Which shirt did you buy?

You: The blue, cotton one — it was cheaper than the red one.
real_life.why: Words like blue, cotton, red describe the shirt (descriptive adjectives), and cheaper compares two shirts — that comparing form is a 'degree of comparison', the heart of this chapter.

rule_box.formula: Comparative uses -er / more … than · Superlative uses -est / most … (the)
rule_box.example: Ravi is taller than Sam, but Amit is the tallest of all.

words.meaning: a unit of sound in a word

quick_test.q: The superlative degree is used when we compare:
quick_test.explanation: Superlatives (tallest, best) compare three or more, and usually take 'the'.

common_mistakes.note: Never use 'more' with an -er comparative — that's a double comparative.

common_mistakes.wrong: Mango is the more sweet of all fruits.
common_mistakes.right: Mango is the sweetest of all fruits.
common_mistakes.note: Comparing all fruits needs the superlative.

reading.passage: The Himalayas are the highest mountains in the world. They are taller than the Alps and far colder in winter. A brave team of climbers reached the snowy peak after a long, difficult journey. Their best moment came when they raised a small flag at the top.

questions.q: Find a superlative adjective in the passage.
questions.answer: highest (also 'best') — the superlative compares all mountains.

questions.q: Find a comparative adjective.
questions.answer: taller (or colder) — it compares the Himalayas with the Alps.

questions.q: Name two descriptive adjectives describing the journey.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences comparing two friends or two cities, using comparative and superlative adjectives.
writing.example: Delhi is bigger than Jaipur, but Jaipur is the cleanest city I know.

'taller' alone is the comparative; 'more taller' is wrong.

micro_quiz.q: 'The garden is green.' The adjective 'green' is:
micro_quiz.explanation: It follows the linking verb 'is', so it is predicative.

options: Iron is more useful than any metal.

challenge.explanation: Comparing one thing with the rest of its group needs 'any other'.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'She is the most cleverest girl in school.'
Transform to positive degree: 'Gold is more precious than silver.'
options: Silver is not as precious as gold.
Silver is more precious than gold.
Gold is as precious as silver.
challenge.explanation: A comparative becomes 'not as … as' in the positive degree.

english.mindmap:
ADJECTIVES
                |
   +------------+------------+
   |            |            |
 KINDS      POSITION      DEGREES
 quality   attributive   positive
 quantity  (before)      compar.-er
 numeral   predicative   super. -est
 demonstr. (after verb)  more/most
 possess.               irregular
revision: An adjective describes a noun or pronoun
Kinds: descriptive, quantitative, numeral, demonstrative, possessive, interrogative
Degrees: positive, comparative (-er/more … than), superlative (-est/most … the)
Never use double forms like 'more taller' or 'most cleverest'
